key_insight: Curvature-Scaled SAM controls gradient distortion under generalized smoothness, enabling convergence guarantees where standard SAM can cycle and unnormalized SAM can diverge.
engineering_relevance: Curvature-aware scaling offers a principled way to stabilize sharpness-aware training beyond conventional smoothness assumptions.
method: Measure how perturbations change the gradient using relative gradient distortion.
Scale both the gradient-aligned perturbation and descent step using curvature upper bounds.
Prove deterministic O(1/T) stationarity and convex function-gap rates, plus linear convergence under the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition.
evidence_signal: Minibatch computer vision experiments show competitive performance, with the (H0,H1) variant attaining the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four tested settings against tuned SAM and USAM baselines.
watch_item: The guarantees are deterministic and depend on suitable curvature upper bounds; practical minibatch training requires choosing or estimating these bounds.
paper_title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness
